safety_observation.name: safety_observation
safety_observation.description: A safety observation refers to any recorded note or report about workplace behaviors, conditions, or practices that may impact health and safety. These observations are typically made by workers, supervisors, or safety personnel during routine checks or daily activities, and can include both positive and negative findings related to safety compliance or risks.
examples: Observed all workers wearing required PPE in the welding area.
Noted that emergency exits were clear and unobstructed during shift.
Identified a missing guard on the conveyor belt during routine inspection.
Observed forklift operator following proper speed limits in the warehouse.
Noticed a spill in the loading dock promptly cleaned up by staff.

near_miss.name: near_miss
near_miss.description: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage but had the potential to do so. In HSE, near misses are critical to report and analyze because they reveal underlying hazards or unsafe conditions that could lead to future incidents if not addressed.
examples: A falling tool narrowly missed a worker passing below.
Forklift reversed into a walkway but stopped before hitting anyone.
Chemical container slipped but was caught before spilling.
Worker tripped over a hose but regained balance without falling.
Overhead load swung out of control but did not strike any equipment.

incident.name: incident
incident.description: An incident is any unplanned event that results in or could have resulted in injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm. In HSE, incidents are formally reported and investigated to identify root causes and prevent recurrence.
examples: Worker sustained a laceration while using a box cutter.
Forklift struck a storage rack causing minor property damage.
Employee slipped on wet floor and sprained ankle.
Chemical spill required evacuation of the lab area.
Fire alarm triggered due to electrical short in equipment.

hazard_report.name: hazard_report
hazard_report.description: A hazard report documents the identification of a potential source of harm or danger in the workplace. These reports are used to alert management and safety teams to risks that need to be assessed and controlled before they cause incidents.
examples: Reported exposed wiring near the main switchboard.
Identified unguarded machinery in the production area.
Noted oil spill on the workshop floor as a slip hazard.
Reported blocked fire extinguisher access.
Observed damaged handrail on the stairs.

environmental_observation.name: environmental_observation
environmental_observation.description: An environmental observation records any condition, event, or behavior that may impact the environment, such as pollution, waste, or resource use. In HSE, these observations help monitor compliance with environmental standards and identify areas for improvement.
examples: Observed oil leaking from equipment onto the ground.
Noted improper disposal of chemical containers in waste bins.
Identified excessive dust emissions from the crusher area.
Reported noise levels exceeding permitted limits near the compressor.
Observed recycling bins overflowing in the break area.

quality_issue.name: quality_issue
quality_issue.description: A quality issue refers to any observation or report of a product, process, or service not meeting required standards or specifications. In HSE, quality issues can have safety or environmental implications if defective materials or processes lead to hazards.
examples: Found welds not meeting inspection criteria on pressure vessel.
Reported incorrect labeling on chemical drums.
Identified faulty safety harnesses in equipment storage.
Observed paint peeling from newly coated surfaces.
Noted missing documentation for batch release.

maintenance_request.name: maintenance_request
maintenance_request.description: A maintenance request is a formal or informal notification to repair, service, or inspect equipment, infrastructure, or safety systems. In HSE, timely maintenance requests help prevent equipment failures that could lead to safety incidents or environmental harm.
examples: Requested repair of leaking valve in the pump room.
Submitted work order for malfunctioning emergency lighting.
Reported broken guardrail on loading dock for maintenance.
Requested inspection of overhead crane after unusual noise.
Notified maintenance about faulty fire alarm panel.

unsafe_condition.name: unsafe_condition
unsafe_condition.description: An unsafe condition is any physical state or environmental factor in the workplace that increases the risk of injury, illness, or damage. Reporting unsafe conditions is essential in HSE to enable corrective actions before incidents occur.
examples: Found wet floor with no warning signs in hallway.
Observed missing machine guards on press.
Noted poor lighting in stairwell.
Identified exposed nails on wooden pallets.
Reported blocked emergency exit door.

unsafe_act.name: unsafe_act
unsafe_act.description: An unsafe act is any behavior or action by a person that increases the likelihood of an accident or injury. In HSE, unsafe acts are observed and reported to address risky behaviors and reinforce safe work practices.
examples: Worker climbed ladder without using fall protection.
Employee bypassed machine safety interlock.
Observed operator not wearing required eye protection.
Worker used forklift to lift personnel without cage.
Employee smoked in a designated no-smoking area.

month.name: month
month.description: In HSE analytics, 'month' refers to a calendar period of approximately 30 days used for tracking, reporting, and analyzing safety observations, incidents, and trends. Monthly aggregation helps identify recurring issues, monitor compliance, and evaluate the effectiveness of safety interventions over shorter timeframes. Typical events include monthly safety audits, incident counts, and hazard reports summarized for each month.
examples: Five near misses were reported in the month of March.
Monthly safety inspection completed for April.
There were two recordable injuries last month.
Monthly hazard observations increased compared to February.
PPE compliance was reviewed for the month.

quarter.name: quarter
quarter.description: In HSE, 'quarter' denotes a three-month period (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4) used for summarizing and analyzing safety performance, trends, and compliance on a broader scale than monthly reporting. Quarterly reviews help identify patterns, assess progress on safety initiatives, and support regulatory or management reporting requirements. Events include quarterly incident summaries, trend analyses, and safety performance reviews.
examples: Quarterly incident rate decreased in Q2.
Quarterly safety meeting held to review trends.
There were eight environmental spills reported last quarter.
Quarterly audit findings were discussed with the team.
Quarterly near miss reports showed improvement.

year.name: year
year.description: In HSE, 'year' refers to a 12-month period used for comprehensive analysis and reporting of safety performance, incident rates, and compliance with regulations. Annual data helps organizations evaluate long-term trends, set safety goals, and fulfill legal or corporate reporting obligations. Events include yearly incident summaries, annual safety reviews, and year-over-year comparisons.
examples: Annual safety report shows a reduction in lost time injuries.
There were 15 recordable incidents last year.
Yearly environmental audit completed in December.
Year-to-date near miss count is lower than previous years.
Annual review of hazard observations conducted.

production.name: production
production.description: In HSE, the production department refers to the area responsible for manufacturing, assembly, or processing of goods. Observations here often involve machine safety, process hazards, line stoppages, and worker behaviors on the shop floor. Typical events include equipment malfunctions, unsafe work practices, or exposure to hazardous materials during production activities.
examples: Operator bypassed machine guard during shift on the assembly line.
Spill of coolant observed near production equipment.
Worker not wearing hearing protection in the manufacturing area.
Conveyor belt emergency stop was blocked by materials.
Unlabeled chemical container found in the production zone.

maintenance.name: maintenance
maintenance.description: The maintenance department handles the repair, servicing, and upkeep of equipment and facilities. HSE observations here often relate to lockout/tagout procedures, working at heights, confined space entry, and tool safety. Incidents may involve improper isolation, slips during repairs, or missing PPE during maintenance tasks.
examples: Technician entered confined space without gas test in maintenance area.
Lockout/tagout procedure not followed during pump repair.
Oil spill left uncleaned after equipment servicing.
Missing guard on grinder in maintenance workshop.
Worker used ladder with damaged rung during maintenance task.

quality.name: quality
quality.description: The quality department oversees product standards, inspections, and compliance with regulations. HSE observations here may involve unsafe sampling practices, improper handling of test chemicals, or ergonomic risks during inspections. Events can include exposure to hazardous substances or unsafe storage of quality control samples.
examples: Inspector handled samples without gloves in quality lab.
Spilled solvent not cleaned up in QC area.
Ergonomic risk observed during repetitive testing procedure.
Blocked emergency exit in quality control office.
Unlabeled reagent stored in quality assurance cabinet.

logistics.name: logistics
logistics.description: The logistics department manages the movement, storage, and distribution of materials and products. HSE issues here often involve vehicle safety, manual handling, loading dock hazards, and traffic management. Observations may include unsafe forklift operation, blocked walkways, or improper stacking of goods.
examples: Forklift operated at excessive speed in loading area.
Pallets stacked unsafely in logistics zone.
Delivery truck blocked emergency access route.
Worker lifted heavy box without assistance in shipping area.
Spill of oil near loading dock not reported.

administration.name: administration
administration.description: The administration department covers office-based staff and support functions such as HR, finance, and management. HSE observations here typically relate to office ergonomics, fire safety, slips and trips, and emergency preparedness. Incidents may include blocked fire exits, poor workstation setup, or electrical hazards in office areas.
examples: Blocked fire exit in administration corridor.
Loose electrical cable caused trip hazard in office.
Improper chair height led to ergonomic complaint.
Unattended coffee spill in admin break room.
Emergency evacuation plan missing from administration area.

safety.name: safety
safety.description: The safety department is responsible for implementing and monitoring health and safety policies, conducting audits, and ensuring compliance. Observations here may include unsafe practices during safety inspections, missing signage, or gaps in emergency response readiness. Events often involve safety walkthroughs, training sessions, or incident investigations.
examples: Safety signage missing in high-risk area during inspection.
Fire extinguisher found discharged during safety audit.
Emergency drill not conducted as scheduled by safety team.
PPE compliance not enforced during safety walkthrough.
Incident investigation report incomplete in safety office.

engineering.name: engineering
engineering.description: The engineering department designs, modifies, and oversees technical systems, equipment, and processes. HSE observations here may involve design-related hazards, unsafe modifications, or risks during commissioning and testing. Events can include inadequate guarding on new equipment or lack of risk assessment for engineering changes.
examples: New machine installed without proper guarding by engineering.
No risk assessment conducted for process modification.
Temporary wiring left exposed after engineering test.
Engineering team entered restricted area without permit.
Design change increased manual handling risk.

warehouse.name: warehouse
warehouse.description: The warehouse department is responsible for storing raw materials, components, and finished goods. HSE issues here often involve manual handling, racking safety, slips and trips, and vehicle-pedestrian interactions. Observations may include blocked aisles, unsafe stacking, or improper use of lifting equipment.
examples: Aisle blocked by pallets in warehouse.
Worker climbed racking to retrieve item.
Spill not cleaned up in warehouse storage area.
Forklift reversed without spotter in warehouse.
Damaged shelving reported in warehouse zone.

operations.name: operations
operations.description: The operations department oversees the day-to-day running of core business activities, often integrating production, logistics, and support functions. HSE observations here may cover cross-functional risks, process upsets, or coordination issues affecting safety. Events can include process deviations, communication breakdowns, or unsafe handovers between shifts.
examples: Shift handover missed critical safety information in operations.
Process deviation not reported to operations supervisor.
Operations team failed to isolate equipment before maintenance.
Unclear responsibilities led to unsafe condition during operations.
Operations staff not briefed on new emergency procedure.

facility_management.name: facility_management
facility_management.description: Facility management covers the upkeep, safety, and functionality of buildings and infrastructure, including utilities, cleaning, and groundskeeping. HSE observations here often involve building hazards, fire safety, contractor management, and environmental risks. Incidents may include blocked emergency exits, unsafe contractor practices, or poor housekeeping in common areas.
examples: Emergency exit blocked by cleaning equipment in facility corridor.
Contractor worked at height without harness in facility area.
Leaking pipe reported in facility management zone.
Poor lighting in facility stairwell created trip hazard.
Housekeeping standards not met in facility common area.
